core_obligations: Consider the distinguished triangle associated to Z -> Z[x_1,...,x_n] -> Z (proof lines 2899-2908).
Identify the first term with the module of differentials of the polynomial ring tensor Z using the polynomial algebra lemma (proof lines 2909-2911).
Use the vanishing lemma for L_{Z/Z} (proof lines 2912-2913).
Conclude that only one cohomology group survives and identify it with I/I^2 by the surjection lemma (proof lines 2914-2915).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for the map A = Z[x_1,...,x_n] -> B = Z sending each x_i to 0, with I = (x_1,...,x_n), the cotangent complex L_{B/A} is quasi-isomorphic to I/I^2[1] (source lines 2889-2895). The proof uses the fundamental distinguished triangle for the composition Z -> Z[x_1,...,x_n] -> Z: the first term is computed by the polynomial algebra lemma as the module of differentials of the polynomial ring base changed to Z, the middle term L_{Z/Z} vanishes by the vanishing lemma, so the long exact sequence shows that L_{B/A} has a single nonzero cohomology group, which the surjection lemma identifies as I/I^2 in degree -1.
